STAGE: design decision for round "curvature, per-layer, fix deep collapse".
READ: workspace contains only progress.jsonl (no repo files readable), so the design is driven by the measured chain given in the brief: (holonomy-path-behaviour-rq) l2_distinct_prefixes=1, l3_collision=1.0, full collapse; (GEOCAP-RQ, with straight-through fixed) hard_ER 3.885 vs 16.390 baseline, positive_hit_rate 0.1222 vs 0.0794, l2_prefixes 4236, l3_collision 0.549, refinement 2.82 bits, rejected by the 35% gate; (OCCURV-FIELD-RQ) ER 2.488, hit 0.2629, l2_prefixes 784, l3_collision 0.943, refinement 2.32 bits, rejected.
REASONING: curvature in the FIRST RQ layer is clearly what buys the first-order gain (ER 16.4 -> 2.5-3.9, hit rate up), and the failure is monotone in depth: the same uniform curvature field applied to the deepest, small-norm residual squeezes codewords into a cone and l3 occupancy collapses. Form already used and excluded: two-leg holonomy transport, popularity-derived geodesic capacity radii, per-codeword reach curvature at uniform intensity. The remaining free design axis is a LAYER-VARYING geometry combined with a behaviour term whose SIGN is layer-scheduled (attract at coarse layers, repel at the finest layer) plus an explicit occupancy capacity at the finest codebook, all inside one cost matrix that also feeds the assignment.
CHOICE: DUALRAMP-CAPRQ - kappa_l = kappa0*(L-l)/(L-1) so layers 1,2,3 get kappa0, kappa0/2, 0 (deep layer Euclidean, as demanded); behaviour mass enters the same cost matrix per (item,codeword) pair, complement mass with attraction at l=1,2 and branch-alternative (substitute) mass with repulsion at l=3; layer 3 additionally gets a capacity-balanced hard assignment (each codeword used ceil(B/K) times) so l3 occupancy cannot collapse; straight-through and the Euclidean tangent codevector for reconstruction are preserved, and exp_0 of residual and of codebook use the same map at the same curvature (one chart).
CONSTANTS derived only: kappa0 = 1/median||z-mean||^2 from the first batch (detached), theta=0.1*mean curvature-distance (documented default times a measured scale), clip 3, Sinkhorn 3 iters, commit 0.25 (baseline), EMA eta=1e-3, 50-step behaviour warmup, capacity ceil(B/K). No sweep, no ablation arm trained, one run.
OPEN: whether capacity balancing raises hard ER above 4 (main risk) and whether branch repulsion actually drives l3_collision under 0.35 in a single run.

IDEA: dualramp-caprq
TITLE: Dual-ramped curvature with sign-flipped behaviour cost and a capacity-balanced deepest RQ layer
MOTIVATION: The measured chain shows curvature in the first RQ layer buys the first-order gain (valid_l1_hard_er 16.39 -> 2.49/3.89, positive_hit_rate 0.079 -> 0.12/0.26) but the same uniform curvature applied at every layer crushes the deepest codebook (l3_collision 0.549 and 0.943, i.e. 55-94% of items share one level-3 code), which blocks the 35% gate and therefore Stage3. The problem is asymmetry: coarse SIDs want to be pulled together by co-consumption so prefixes are predictable, fine SIDs must be pushed apart so substitutable next items stay distinguishable and the deep codebook stays occupied.
NOVELTY: Curvature is not one field but a LAYER RAMP that reaches exactly zero at the deepest RQ layer, and the behaviour term flips sign with depth (complement/transition attraction at layers 1-2, branch-alternative repulsion at layer 3), both entering the SAME cost matrix that drives assignment. On top of that the deepest layer gets an explicit capacity (each codeword used ceil(B/K) times) so occupancy cannot collapse by construction. This is not cross-chart holonomy transport, not popularity-derived area-law radii, and not a per-codeword reach curvature at uniform intensity; geometry and behaviour are per-layer and per-pair inside one assignment operator.
CHANGE: The RQ residual and the codebook of layer l are both pushed through the same exponential map exp_0^{kappa_l} into one Poincare chart with layer-specific curvature [kappa0, kappa0/2, 0], the squared Poincare distance minus a scaled per-(item,codeword) behaviour mass forms the cost, and the code index is the capacitated argmax of a transport plan at the last layer (plain argmin at layers 1-2); reconstruction still adds the tangent codevector with a straight-through estimator.
SPECIFICATION: Params/widths: L=3 codebooks C_l in R^{256 x d} (K=256, d=encoder width, as baseline, not swept); frozen buffers kappa0=1/median_b||z_b-mean(z)||^2 from step 0, kappa_l=kappa0*(L-l)/(L-1) -> [k0,k0/2,0]; epsilon_l = median_{i,j} m_ij^l (per step, detached); tau_l = 0.1 * mean_{i,j} m_ij^l (per step, detached); beta=0.25; eta=1e-3; T=3 Sinkhorn iterations; behaviour warmup 50 steps with tau_l=0; capacity cap=ceil(B/K).
Per step: r=z=Enc(x) [B=1024,d]; for l=1..3: Rt=exp0^{\kappa_l}(r), Ct=exp0^{\kappa_l}(C_l), m_ij=dkappa_l(Rt_i,Ct_j)^2; B_ij = A_ij(l<=2) or R_ij(l=3); uhat=detach(clip(B_ij/(mean_j B_ij+1e-8),-3,3)); C_ij = m_ij - s_l*tau_l*uhat with s=[+1,+1,-1]; l<3: k_i=argmin_j C_ij; l=3: P=log-domain Sinkhorn(-C/eps_3, rows 1/B, cols 1/K, T=3), then capacitated greedy over ascending C_ij using -log P only to break ties, cap=4 per codeword; q_i=C_l[k_i]; cb_loss_l = 0.25*dkappa_l(sg[Rt_i],Ct_{k_i})^2 for kappa_l>0 else ||sg[r_i]-C_l[k_i]||^2; r <- r + (q_i - r).detach(); z_q=sum_l q_l; total loss = ||x-Dec(z_q)||^2 + sum_l [||sg[r_l]-C_l[k]||^2 + beta*||r_l-sg[C_l[k]]||^2] + sum_l cb_loss_l.
COST: One run, 3000 Stage-2 epochs x 24 steps x B=1024 on 24556 items, no extra forward pass, no extra loss weight. Extra work per step vs baseline quantizer: exp/log on B+K vectors per layer (negligible), 3-layer curved distance (same B*K*d FLOP count as baseline, ~25M MAC), one 3-iteration Sinkhorn at layer 3 (3*B*K = 0.8M) and one B*K sort (0.26M elements, ~1-3 ms GPU). Estimated +3% to +6% wall-clock per step, i.e. ~1.05x the frozen Stage-2 budget. One-off CPU precompute of the

sparse transition and branch tables over 24556 items (~0.5M sparse entries, a few minutes).
HYPOTHESIS: If deep collapse (not curvature in general) is the blocker, then the layer ramp (kappa_3=0) plus layer-3 branch repulsion plus capacity ceil(B/K)=4 per codeword per layer drops l3_collision from 0.549/0.943 to below the 0.35 gate while valid_l1_hard_er stays <= 4 and positive_hit_rate >= 0.12, keeping refinement >= 2.3 bits and l2_distinct_prefixes >= 4000, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.0638 (best so far) with >0.065 the target. Observed by the per-layer usage entropy and collision diagnostics plus the single Stage3 evaluation; falsified if l3_collision stays >0.35, or ER >4, or hit rate <0.12, or test_R@10 <= 0.0638.
RISKS: Capacity balancing at layer 3 may force semantically poor code choices and push hard ER above 4 (the main risk); shallow complement attraction may re-inflate level-1/level-2 collisions and undo the curvature gain; the EMA prefix table lags early in training so the behaviour cost is noise for the first hundreds of steps; sparse predecessor counts are head-item dominated so repulsion may concentrate on popular items; the B*K sort adds a small host-device sync per step; single-seed noise of the order of a few 1e-3 on recall could hide a real but small gain.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-to-item transitions (next-item co-consumption) and user-interest branching (items sharing the same predecessor set but not linked by a transition), both as per-(item,codeword) masses, computed only from the Stage-2 training split.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training sequences only: N(a->b) = count of consecutive (a,b) pairs; row-stochastic w(a,b)=N(a->b)/sum_b' N(a->b'). Complement mass A_l(i,j)= sum_{n in Top50(i) by w(i,.)} w(i,n)*1[pi_l(n)=j]. Branch mass: Pred(i) = top 10 predecessors by N(s->i); for pairs (i,n) with N(i->n)+N(n->i)=0, b(i,n)= sum_{s in Pred(i) cap Pred(n)} min(w(s,i),w(s,n)), keep top 16 by b, normalise so sum_n b(i,n)=1; R_l(i,j)= sum_n b(i,n)*1[pi_l(n)=j]. pi_l is the EMA (eta=1e-3) of the model's own hard training assignments, stop-gradient.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Both tables are built once at step 0 from the Stage-2 training split only (asserted on the split name before load, hard failure otherwise); pi_l is an EMA of assignments produced on training mini-batches during the run. Validation and test interactions are never read, never counted and never fed into any SID, cost, curvature, capacity or codebook; the validation split is touched only by the post-hoc diagnostic reporting, after the SIDs of the epoch are frozen.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Trainable-free fixed negative curvature per layer, kappa_l in {kappa0, kappa0/2, 0} with kappa0 = 1/median||z-mean||^2; the operations are the exponential map exp_0^kappa(v)=tanh(sqrt(kappa)||v||)/(sqrt(kappa)||v||)*v, its inverse log map, and the Poincare distance d_kappa(u,v)=(1/sqrt(kappa))*arcosh(1+2*kappa*||u-v||^2/((1-kappa*||u||^2)(1-kappa*||v||^2))); at kappa_3=0 all three reduce to identity / Euclidean norm.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the RQ quantization itself, at the assignment step of every layer, and (through the scale-matched commit term) in the codebook parameter update; the layer-3 residual is the Euclidean residual of the curved layers 1-2, so the curvature still reaches layer 3 through the residual chain even though its own metric is flat.
COUPLING PATH: One cost matrix per layer whose metric is the curved distance and whose additive term is the be

haviour mass of that same layer; the argmin (or capacitated transport argmax at layer 3) of that single matrix picks the codeword, the codeword then sets the next residual, and the assignment statistics pi_l that the behaviour mass is gathered through are the model's own curved decisions. Removing behaviour (tau=0) changes which code wins; removing curvature (kappa0=0) changes the metric inside the same expression and therefore also which code wins; neither is a side loss.
COUPLING EQUATION: C_ij^(l) = d_{kappa_l}( exp_0^{kappa_l}(r_i) , exp_0^{kappa_l}(c_j) )^2 - s_l * tau_l * clip( B_l(i,j) / mean_j B_l(i,j) , -3 , +3 ), with kappa = [kappa0, kappa0/2, 0], s = [+1, +1, -1], B_l = A_l for l<=2 and R_l for l=3, tau_l = 0.1 * mean_ij m_ij^(l).
OBSERVABLES: l3_collision must fall below 0.35 (was 0.549 / 0.943 / 1.0); per-layer code usage entropy near log 256 at layer 3 (capacity guarantees 4 items per codeword per batch); valid_l1_hard_er <= 4 and not back to the 16.39 baseline band; positive_hit_rate >= 0.12; refinement >= 2.3 bits; level2_distinct_prefixes >= 4000; per-layer codebook gradient norms and row-wise commit distances shift with the layer ramp; final Stage3 test_recall@10 above 0.065.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: tau_l = 0 for all layers, i.e. the pure layer-ramped curved-metric capacity-balanced assignment (switch exists as a config flag, not trained this round).
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa0 = 0 so kappa_l = 0 for every layer, exp/log become identity and d_kappa becomes the Euclidean distance, while the behaviour masses, the sign schedule, the capacity and the straight-through path stay unchanged (switch exists, not trained this round).
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full coupled run, kappa = [kappa0, kappa0/2, 0] with behaviour attraction at layers 1-2, branch repulsion at layer 3 and capacity-balanced layer 3; this is the only arm trained.
SPEC EQUATIONS: kappa0 = 1/median_b ||z_b - mean(z)||^2 (step 0, detached); kappa_l = kappa0*(3-l)/2; exp0^k(v) = tanh(sqrt(k)||v||)/(sqrt(k)||v||+1e-12)*v (identity if k=0); dk(u,v) as above (||u-v||^2 if k=0); m_ij^l = dk(Rt_i,Ct_j)^2; uhat = clip(B_l(i,j)/(mean_j B_l(i,j)+1e-8),-3,3).detach(); C_ij^l = m_ij^l - s_l*tau_l*uhat, tau_l = 0.1*mean_ij m_ij^l; k_i = argmin_j C_ij^l for l<3; for l=3: K_ij = exp(-C_ij/eps_3), log-domain Sinkhorn T=3 with row marginal 1/B and column marginal 1/K, then order pairs by (C_ij, -log P_ij) ascending and greedily assign each item to its best codeword with remaining capacity cap=ceil(B/K); q_i=C_l[k_i]; r_{l+1} = r_l + (q_i - r_l).detach(); L = ||x-Dec(sum_l q^{(l)})||^2 + sum_l [||sg(r_l)-q^{(l)}||^2 + 0.25*||r_l-sg(q^{(l)})||^2 + commit_l], commit_l = 0.25*dk(Rt_l,Ct_{k})^2 if kappa_l>0 else ||sg(r_l)-q||^2.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: batch of encoder latents z in R^{B x d} (B=1024, d = encoder width), codebooks C_1..C_3 in R^{256 x d}, frozen kappa0, per-step epsilon_3, tau_l and behaviour masses A_l, R_l gathered for the batch from the training-only sparse tables and the stop-gradient prefix EMA pi_l, and the reconstruction target x. Outputs: hard code indices k_1,k_2,k_3 per item (the SIDs consumed by Stage 3), the quantized tangent vector z_q = sum_l C_l[k_l] for the decoder, per-layer commit values for the codebook update, and diagnostics (per-layer usage histogram, entropy, collision/prefix counts).
SAFEGUARDS: assert B >= K and cap >= 1; kappa_l >= 0 always, with an exact Euclid-ean branch at kappa_l = 0 (limit forms) so layer 3 never divides by zero; cla

mp the ball norm to (1-1e-5)/sqrt(kappa) so tanh saturation cannot zero the distance denominator; compute distances with the denominator floored at 1e-6; log-domain Sinkhorn with row-max subtraction and a fixed 3 iterations, epsilon_3 floored at 1e-6; all buffer statistics detached and never backpropagated; tau set to 0 for the first 50 steps and whenever the prefix EMA is not yet populated; a global non-finite guard that replaces a non-finite cost row by the pure Euclidean distance row (with a logged counter, not a tuned fallback); capacity greedy uses stable double-key sorting so it is deterministic for a fixed batch; behaviour-table build asserts the training split name and fails hard otherwise; no validation/test data is read inside any of these paths.
END IDEA
